title: Craft Beer 6-pack

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; no past closure data, but typical 1-day loss in a 6-day week reduces sales by ~17% (1/6); adjusted for noise and lack of historical data

adjustment.analysis: The store closure on Monday (2026-11-09) reduces demand for the week. Historical data shows no direct closure effect, but the product's ordinary week noise is ±37%, and the baseline already reflects recent trend decay (trend_13_vs_prior_13_pct = -15.7%). The planner note is the only driver. No promotion, price change, or event. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, consistent with no known promotion. The closure likely cuts sales by ~15–20% (one weekday lost, typical impact for a 6-day week). Noise-adjusted estimate shrinks toward 1.0 due to low evidence, but the closure is a clear driver. Downside spread widened slightly to reflect uncertainty. Median adjusted downward. No other drivers.

  median 140.8 | 5%-95%: 66.5 - 224.4 | 10%-90%: 75.4 - 185.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-37% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
